observed_title: Distribution functions, extremal limits and optimal transport

read_ranges.scope: Read the complete extracted text from title/abstract through references, including all sections and theorem proofs. Rendered original PDF pages 8, 9, and 14 with PyMuPDF to verify the transport duality/cycle formulas and the dyadic approximation theorem; page 14 rendering confirmed the grid denominator is 2^n.

topic_relevance.A03: direct, narrow: proves optimizer existence/stability for probability couplings, including subsequential convergence of optimizers for compact uniform-marginal problems and weakly converging marginals. It does not treat concentration-compactness or mass escape on noncompact domains; transfer is limited to tight families and continuous costs.

definitions.name: Copula as a probability measure with uniform marginals
definitions.statement: In the paper’s two-dimensional setting, a copula corresponds to a Borel probability measure on [0,1]^2 whose two marginals are uniform; the fixed-marginal transport problem is therefore an optimization over such couplings.

definitions.name: Kantorovich admissible plans
definitions.statement: ADM(μ,ν) is the set of Borel probability measures γ on X×Y whose marginals are μ and ν; the relaxed transport objective is ∫c(x,y) dγ.

definitions.name: c-cyclic monotonicity
definitions.statement: A set Γ⊂X×Y is c-cyclically monotone when every finite cycle in Γ satisfies Σ c(x_n,y_n) ≤ Σ c(x_{n+1},y_n), with x_{N+1}=x_1.

definitions.name: Dyadic cellwise cost envelopes
definitions.statement: For a continuous c on [0,1]^2, divide the square into 2^n-by-2^n cells and define lower/upper step costs by the cellwise minimum and maximum of c. The corresponding maximizing couplings approximate the continuous problem’s value.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 3.1 (existence of a Kantorovich optimizer; cited result)
assumptions: X,Y are Polish spaces as in the transport setup.
The cost c is lower semicontinuous.
theorem_cards.statement: The paper states that problem (8), minimizing ∫c dγ over ADM(μ,ν), has a minimizer.
proof_steps: 作者陈述：this is quoted as Theorem 1.5 from Ambrosio–Gigli; no proof is supplied in this paper.

核验基础推导：not independently proved here; on the compact uniform-marginal application below, the admissible couplings are weakly compact and continuous costs are bounded, so attainment is consistent with the standard compactness argument.
gaps: The article prints only lower semicontinuity at this point and imports the theorem. Do not export this terse formulation beyond the cited theorem’s full hypotheses without checking the cited source.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 3.4 (optimality characterization by c-cyclic monotonicity; cited result)
assumptions: X,Y are Polish; μ,ν are Borel probability measures.
c is lower semicontinuous and satisfies c(x,y)≥a(x)+b(y), with upper-semicontinuous real-valued a∈L¹(μ), b∈L¹(ν).
theorem_cards.statement: There is a measurable c-cyclically monotone set Γ such that, for any admissible γ, optimality is equivalent to concentration on a c-cyclically monotone set, equality with a c-convex potential almost surely, or concentration on Γ.
proof_steps: 作者陈述：quoted from Villani, Theorem 5.10(ii); this paper does not reprove the equivalence.
核验基础推导：the finite-cycle condition is transcribed and used in the paper’s later proofs; the full equivalence remains a cited theorem.
gaps: The maximization variant changes the sign/convention of c-convexity and is stated separately; do not copy the minimization formula unchanged.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 4.1 (stability under weakly convergent marginals; cited result)
assumptions: μ_n⇒μ and ν_n⇒ν; π_n is an optimizer for transport with marginals μ_n,ν_n.
theorem_cards.statement: There is a subsequence of π_n converging weakly to a transport plan π that optimizes the limiting problem; every convergent subsequence has an optimal limit, so the nonempty cluster-point set consists of optimizers.
proof_steps: 作者陈述：quoted as Theorem 3 from Schachermayer–Teichmann; the present paper supplies no proof.

核验基础推导：weak convergence of marginals makes each marginal sequence tight; the fixed-marginal coupling family is tight by the two-coordinate tail bound, and any weak limit retains its marginals. This verifies the compactness mechanism only, not the full optimality conclusion.
gaps: The cost is required to be nonnegative, continuous, and finite-valued in the quoted statement. The article does not independently establish this theorem or its optimal-value passage.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 4.2 (dyadic cost approximation and subsequential optimizer convergence)
assumptions: The grid consists of 2^n-by-2^n cells; each cell receives the lower or upper envelope of c.
γ_n are maximizing measures for the respective step costs; their marginals remain uniform.
theorem_cards.statement: The lower- and upper-envelope optimum values converge to the supremum for c over copulas, and the corresponding sequence of maximizers has a subsequence converging to a maximizer of the original continuous-cost problem.
proof_steps: 作者陈述：the convergence of values is attributed to Hofer–Iacò [25]; this paper proves the subsequential-optimum claim and explicitly sketches the lower-envelope case.
作者证明：uniform marginals on compact [0,1] make {γ_n} tight, so choose γ_{n_j}⇒γ*. The limit still has uniform marginals.

作者证明：optimality for each step cost gives cyclic inequalities; uniform continuity of c makes them ε-cyclic inequalities for c on sufficiently fine grids. The closed ε-cycle sets and weak convergence of finite product measures pass these inequalities to γ*; letting ε↓0 gives c-cyclical monotonicity.
作者援引：Theorem 3.4 and boundedness of c on [0,1]^2 conclude γ* is optimal.

核验基础推导：the cell width tends to zero and c is uniformly continuous on the compact square; coordinate pushforwards are continuous under weak convergence, so γ* retains both uniform marginals. Rendered PDF p.14 confirms the dyadic grid and envelope definitions.
gaps: The printed proof details the lower-envelope sequence and says the upper case is analogous; the preceding value-convergence claim is imported from [25].
The transfer uses compact support and fixed tight marginals. This does not prove sequential compactness for arbitrary probability measures on a noncompact space.

constant_dependence.explicit: No quantitative concentration or convergence rate is given. In Theorem 4.2, cell diameters shrink as 2^{-n}; uniform continuity of c controls the envelope error, while compactness of [0,1]^2 and fixed uniform marginals supply subsequential compactness. In Theorem 4.1 the relevant assumptions are Polish spaces, nonnegative finite continuous cost, and weak convergence of both marginals.
constant_dependence.dependence: The optimizer-existence/stability conclusion rests on tightness and cost lower-semicontinuity/continuity, not a numerical constant. The compact uniform-marginal setting prevents mass escape; outside it one needs tightness or other coercive/integrability hypotheses.

endpoint_limits.compact_case: For copulas on [0,1]^2 with fixed uniform marginals, every sequence is tight and has weakly convergent subsequences, and Theorem 4.2 identifies the limit of its step-cost optimizers as an optimizer.
endpoint_limits.noncompact_case: The paper does not analyze mass escaping to infinity, concentration profiles, or loss of moment constraints. Theorem 4.1 assumes marginal weak convergence and nonnegative finite continuous cost; it is not a substitute for proving tightness of a free sequence.
endpoint_limits.boundary_and_cost: Theorem 4.2 uses continuous c on the compact square, hence bounded and uniformly continuous. These endpoint protections disappear for discontinuous or unbounded costs.

reusable_methods.method: For a sequence of optimal couplings with convergent marginals, establish tightness from the marginal tails and pass to a weak limit before studying optimality.
reusable_methods.transfer: Then separately verify that the limiting marginals are correct and that the cost functional is lower-semicontinuous or continuous under the selected topology.

reusable_methods.method: Approximate a continuous compact-domain cost by cellwise lower/upper envelopes, solve the discrete coupling problems, and use weak compactness plus approximate cyclic monotonicity to identify a limit optimizer.
reusable_methods.transfer: The scheme relies on uniform continuity and compactness; it provides no mass-escape control on noncompact domains.

reusable_methods.method: Use c-cyclic monotonicity as an optimality certificate for candidate coupling supports.
reusable_methods.transfer: Check the correct sign convention for maximization versus minimization and the theorem’s integrability and finite-value assumptions.
